---
title: "Figure 4 (sim anchor) — the same plane with the distortion read at the simulation truth"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
WHAT THIS IS. `figure_4.Rmd` with ONE thing changed: the distortion half is read from
`battery_sim_G` instead of `battery_pool_G`. Same roster, same data directories, same scale, same
lines, same rows, same layout, same `per_row`. The single knob is `FIG4_ANCHOR <- "sim"`, declared
before the source; `figure_4_common.R` filters the half-B products to that anchor once, at the
source, so nothing else in the composition knows the difference.

The bias half does NOT change and never could: it was always read at theta_sim, because
GDIB = G_bar^-1 * (mean score) and the pooled score vanishes at theta_pool by the stationarity
condition of the joint fit, so a pool-anchored bias is zero by construction for every member.

So this figure is BOTH halves at theta_sim, against `figure_4.Rmd`'s bias-at-sim,
distortion-at-pool.

WHY IT IS WORTH DRAWING. Two reasons, one practical and one that is a question.

The practical one is that the original argument for anchoring the distortion at the optimum has
expired. It was to keep the finite-difference Fisher out of the indefinite region, which is a real
pathology of a numerically differenced Hessian off the maximum. The body has anchored on the
analytic Gaussian Fisher G_bar since the freeze, and G_bar is positive semidefinite by
construction at every theta. There is no numerical reason left to prefer the optimum.

The question is what the pool anchor buys, and it is not obvious that it is neutral. GIDM is a
RATIO OF TWO SCORE VARIANCES, J = Var_true(score) over G_bar = Var_model(score), and a ratio of
variances needs no stationary point to be defined: unlike the sandwich, it is not an asymptotic
statement about an estimator. Both readings are legitimate and they answer different questions.
Two things separate them:

  - At theta_pool every member has REFIT its nuisance parameters, Current_Noise among them. A
    member that under-predicts its own dispersion can absorb the shortfall into the instrumental
    noise and buy calibration with a parameter rather than with a better predictive. At theta_sim
    it cannot: sigma^2 sits at the truth. If that mechanism is real, the pool anchor is
    systematically kinder to the members that have somewhere to hide, and this figure minus
    `figure_4.Rmd` measures how much each one buys. Note the asymmetry it would create in the
    published comparison: LSE runs with Current_Noise FIXED and so cannot make that trade at all,
    while every macro member can.
  - theta_pool DEPENDS ON THE DESIGN. It is the Kullback-Leibler projection under this interval,
    this N_ch and this noise, so every cell of the pool-anchored plane is measured against its own
    anchor, some hundreds of them across the map. theta_sim is the same point in every cell. For a
    figure whose whole job is to read how a quantity varies ACROSS the plane, a moving reference is
    a real interpretive cost.

WHAT TO LOOK AT, in order. First the saturation report `figure_4_common.R` prints: the distortion
scale (DIST_LIN) was built against pool-anchored values, IR 0.97-1.49 and R 0.44-1.82 with NR's
tail out to 3.4e4, and there is no guarantee the sim-anchored field lives in the same range. If it
saturates, the number is printed and the scale is the thing to fix, not the figure. Second whether
the IR column still reaches white, which is the paper's claim and the one reading that must not
depend on the anchor. Third whether the ORDERING of the five members survives; a changed level with
an intact ordering is a much weaker finding than a reordering.

WHAT THIS FIGURE CANNOT DO, and it is the reason the ratio is a separate notebook. Comparing this
plane against `figure_4.Rmd` cell by cell mixes two displacements: the numerator J and the
denominator G_bar BOTH move with the anchor, and a cell that looks unchanged may be two changes
cancelling. Separating them needs the congruence
G_pool^-1/2 . G_sim . G_pool^-1/2 formed per cell, which is `figure_4_pool_sim_ratio.Rmd`. The raw
J and G_bar are on disk as full 6x6 matrices in both batteries
(`Probit_statistics_Moment_statistics_Sum_dlogL` at `statistic == "covariance"` and
`..._Sum_Gaussian_Fisher_Information` at `statistic == "mean"`), so that step needs no re-run
either.

BOOTSTRAP. Each anchor carries its own percentile intervals and this figure uses them exactly as
`figure_4.Rmd` does, through the CI-aware `Dconf`. What is NOT available from disk is an interval
on the DIFFERENCE between the anchors: the two batteries share `seed = 0` and resample vectors of
the same length, so their bootstrap index sets coincide replicate by replicate and a paired
analysis would be the right one, but the CSVs carry only the percentile summaries and not the
per-replicate samples. Point estimates only, for the ratio.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# Identical to figure_4.Rmd, plus the anchor. Both are read by figure_4_common.R at source time.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR", "macro_R", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "LSE", macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
                    macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
FIG4_ANCHOR    <- "sim"
source("figure_4_common.R")
```

```{r layout, include=FALSE}
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# Same two halves as figure_4.Rmd. `bias` is unchanged (it was always sim-anchored); `stat` now
# holds the sim-anchored distortion because figure_4_common.R filtered it there.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "distortion-induced bias", letter = "A",
       data = bias,                                  zf = function(x) x$Bconf),
  list(lab = "information distortion at the truth",  letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "total"),  zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 5.95}
# Same layout as figure_4.Rmd: same column count, same row spans, so the same solved PER_ROW.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.179, out = "Figure_4_sim.pdf")
```

```{r compare, echo=FALSE}
# The two planes side by side as NUMBERS, so the visual reading is checked against one. Medians
# over the seven intervals at noise 0.1, per member and parameter, exactly the reduction
# figure_4.Rmd's header table uses. Dconf is the CI EDGE toward 1, not the point estimate, so a
# 1.000 here means "the interval brackets 1"; `m` is carried alongside for that reason.
cmp <- .fig4_all$stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo %in% ALGOS, comp == "total", noise == "0.1",
                param %in% c("off", "Num_ch_mean")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(param, algo, Num_ch, anchor) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Dconf = median(Dconf), m = median(m), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = anchor, values_from = c(Dconf, m)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(ALGO_LAB[algo], levels = ALGO_LAB[ALGOS])) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(param, algo, Num_ch)
cat("\n=== distortion, median over the 7 intervals, noise 0.1 ===\n")
cat("Dconf = CI edge toward 1 (what the map paints); m = the point estimate\n\n")
print(as.data.frame(cmp), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```
